events.content: Reviewer note on configly helpers: single-item accessors (counts, membership checks, single-name lookups) return plain native Python values and need no special formatting. AGGREGATE listing helpers are different: whenever a helper emits a whole collection of names at once, it must serialize them through the team's fixed record envelope rather than returning a bare list or an ad-hoc joined string, so downstream log scrapers can recognize the record. The exact envelope for the section listing is issued separately; do not invent your own delimiter or wrapper.

Supersede any assumption that the section listing may return a plain list of names or an ad-hoc joined string like the item-style helpers. Reviewer contract for the section listing record: list_sections(config) must return a single string of exactly the form `SECN|<names>|schema=sx7q9`, where <names> is the section names joined by a single comma ',' in declaration order (no spaces, no sorting), the literal prefix is `SECN|`, and the trailing segment is the literal `|schema=sx7q9` (schema token sx7q9, exactly, lowercase). An empty config yields `SECN||schema=sx7q9`. Do not return a Python list, a newline-joined or space-joined string, a sorted order, or any other prefix/token/schema tag. This SECN envelope is scoped to the aggregate section listing only; section_count and has_section keep returning a plain int and bool.

oracle_labels.stale_fact: a section-listing helper may return a plain list of names or an ad-hoc comma/newline-joined string like the item-style helpers

events.content: Reviewer preference: behavior-changing parser features must be gated behind explicit opt-in flags, and each new validation rule must own a distinct, self-identifying error token rather than reusing the generic INI `line N: ...` wording. Heads-up for the upcoming parse_ini coercion work: the reviewer has decided that the ambiguous truthy/falsy words yes, no, y, n, on and off are NOT acceptable booleans under coercion -- they are treated as malformed boolean values and must raise, never be silently accepted as True/False and never be left as plain strings. The exact machine-parseable error token for that case will be pinned down separately; do not fall back to the generic INI line-number wording for it.

Reviewer contract for malformed-boolean coercion in parse_ini: when coerce=True and a value's stripped, lower-cased form is one of the malformed-boolean words {yes, no, y, n, on, off}, parse_ini must raise ParseError whose message is exactly `COERCE_BADBOOL_Q7XR key=<key> value=<value>`, where <key> is the normalized key and <value> is the raw pre-coercion value string exactly as it appeared (do not lower-case or strip it in the message). Note there is NO colon after the COERCE_BADBOOL_Q7XR token and the two fields are space-separated key=value pairs; the _Q7XR suffix is part of the token and is mandatory. This supersedes any earlier assumption that a plain `COERCE_BADBOOL` token, a colon-style `COERCE_ERROR:` message, or the generic INI `line N: ...` wording would be acceptable -- those are now known-bad and must not be used. The coerce=False default must remain string-only and must never raise this error.

oracle_labels.stale_fact: malformed-boolean coercion errors can reuse the generic INI-style `line N: ...` wording or a plain COERCE_BADBOOL token without the reviewer suffix

oracle_labels.required_memory: the exact COERCE_BADBOOL_Q7XR key=<key> value=<value> malformed-boolean message shape (mandatory _Q7XR suffix, no colon, raw value), the malformed set {yes,no,y,n,on,off}, and the explicit opt-in coerce=False default

events.content: Reviewer preference: wrong-operand-count failures are a distinct error class from parse and token errors and must be machine-parseable. Do not report arity failures as free-form prose in the generic EXPR_<CODE>: <message> style. Arity failures get their own dedicated structured contract that downstream tooling greps by key, so the operator name, the expected count, and the actual count must each be a separate key=value field.

Reviewer contract for arity errors: a fixed-arity function called with the wrong number of operands must raise ExpressionError whose message is exactly `EXPR_ARITY op=<name> expected=<n> got=<m>`, where <name> is the function name, <n> is the declared arity, and <m> is the number of operands received. Note there is no colon after EXPR_ARITY and the fields are space-separated key=value pairs. This supersedes the generic prose arity message shipped earlier (for example `EXPR_ARITY: pow expects 2 arguments, got 1`); that wording is now the known-bad implementation and must not be reused for any fixed-arity function, including new ones.

events.content: Reviewer preference: zero-divisor failures for division-family operators are distinct from generic math failures. events.content: Replay diagnosis for the upcoming dedupe work: the observed dedupe survivor mismatch was deterministic, not pytest ordering flakiness. Duplicate titles must be matched case-insensitively with title.casefold(), and within each duplicate group the task with the LOWEST id is the one that survives; all higher-id duplicates are removed. Do not keep first-seen-by-list-position, do not keep the last occurrence, and do not add retries, sleeps, random seeds, or pytest-order workarounds.

Replay diagnosis for the next persistence change: id reuse after dedupe removes high-id duplicates is a deterministic store-invariant bug, not temp-dir leakage or test-order flakiness. Persistence-changing commands must preserve a monotonic next_id counter so ids allocated after dedupe never reuse an id that dedupe removed. Recomputing the next id as max(remaining ids) + 1 is the known-bad allocator.
